transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Zephyr CTO), Derek Ruiz (Lead ML Eng, Zephyr), Priya Nair (Security), Omar Haddad (SWE), Speaker 1 (Finance?)

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Redwood team gave high-level of deployed options and Dave — sorry Samir — walked through SDK and proxy options. Customer asked about LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors, whether the Redwood SDK plays nicely with a gateway or if we should use a sidecar, and how rate limiting and quotas map to per-team usage. Security questions covered KMS, SSO, and audit logs.

[00:00] Samir Patel (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to orient quickly — i'll hand off to leah for the technical run through, and we can sync on security/ops.
[00:14] Leah Gomez (Redwood SE): thanks samir, hi maya, derek — quick agenda: 1) how you plan to call the API today, 2) SDK / LangChain / LlamaIndex patterns, 3) gateway / proxy / sidecar options, 4) rate limits / quotas + throttling, 5) observability hooks and logs, then q&a and next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Maya Chen (Zephyr): yep sounds good. quick context: we're a mid-size infra company, lotsa customer support automation and internal search. currently using a mix of OpenAI and some in-house models; interested in Redwood for predictable latency and possibly bringing a dedicated fleet. timeline is Q3 pilot then possible prod in Q4.
[00:46] Derek Ruiz (Zephyr): our stack — python microservices, heavy use of LangChain for retrieval-augmented generation in support flows, and some LlamaIndex for document indexing. we also have an api gateway (kong) and a separate ml-proxy in front of model calls.
[01:05] Leah: great, that helps. on the SDK side — Redwood has first-class SDKs for Python, Node, and a REST API. Python SDK plays nicely with LangChain and LlamaIndex; we have example connectors. can you share how you instantiate llm objects today? rough code is fine.
[01:23] Derek: yeah we create an OpenAI wrapper in LangChain today — so the question is do we replace that with RedwoodSDK LLM wrapper or do we keep our proxy and just forward?
[01:35] Leah: both are valid. 1) You can swap the LLM in LangChain to use our SDK directly — minimal changes, direct auth via api key or token. 2) If you need traffic control and internal auditing, keep the gateway/proxy and point it to Redwood's hosted endpoints or dedicated endpoint. when you said ml-proxy, is that doing auth/tokening right now?
[01:56] Omar Haddad (Zephyr): yeah the proxy does auth and does some pre/post processing; we also do sampling for logs. putting Redwood behind that is what we wanted to confirm — especially 1) can we route to Hosted vs Dedicated endpoints behind the proxy, 2) how session affinity/caching would work.
[02:14] Leah: absolutely. for hosted you hit api.redwood.ai (or region-specific) and for Dedicated we can expose a dedicated endpoint or private VPC peering. many customers put a proxy in front and keep their existing auth flow. small caveat: if you want prefix KV cache to be effective across requests you may prefer to let Redwood handle caching rather than double-proxying.
[02:38] Priya Nair (Security): quick sec Q — for Dedicated and Private what does the network topology look like? we need diagrams for peering, firewall rules, and whether the control plane sees ephemeral data.
[02:51] Samir: yep we'll share a network topology doc. Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in our infra and optional VPC peering; Private: customer-managed control plane with on-prem/off-cloud options. data in flight is TLS, at rest we can integrate with your KMS or allow Redwood-managed keys. control plane metadata is minimal; we can enable audit logging and SIEM exports.
[03:10] Maya: vocabulary check — when you say "control plane" are you still storing logs or transcripts in hosted Redwood? we need to avoid PII retention for some customers.
[03:20] Leah: fair — we have controls: you can opt out of transcript retention on Hosted, or with Dedicated we can configure retention policies and KMS so logs are encrypted with your key; Private means logs are within your VPC/on-prem. we'll send the SOC2 and data-retention checklist.
[03:37] Derek: on LangChain integrations — do you have examples for streaming tokens and callback handlers? we rely a lot on streaming to UI and partial generations.
[03:47] Leah: yes, streaming is supported in SDKs; LangChain callbacks can attach to our streaming client; we have a sample where LangChain's LLMChain uses Redwood's stream generator and the callbacks hook into partial tokens. we'll share the repo snippet.
[04:05] [Ambient noise / crosstalk] Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
[04:21] Leah: regarding LlamaIndex, we have an adapter and example indexer that pushes embeddings to Redwood embeddings endpoint; many customers use our embeddings for vector stores or push to Pinecone/Weaviate. note: embedding model choices and dimensionality vary and we'll include recommended model + quantization guidance.
[04:45] Maya: how do you do rate limits and quotas? we want per-team quotas and soft vs hard limits.
[04:54] Samir: we offer per-API-key quotas, and for Dedicated you can have route-level policies. quotas can be soft (throttled with warnings) or hard (reject with 429). for multi-team orgs we recommend per-service keys or token-scoped policies with RBAC in the Console.
[05:12] Priya: do you support SSO / SAML + SCIM? we need to provision a handful of developer and production users and integrate with our Okta.
[05:20] Samir: yes, Console supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for provisioning; RBAC roles map to Console permissions. we'll share the SSO integration guide.
[05:34] Derek: observability hooks — we want request tracing and per-request token counts and latency breakdowns by model. can we push traces to our datadog or jaeger?
[05:45] Leah: telemetry options: 1) Console-level dashboards with per-route/model metrics (token counts, cost, lat p50/p95) 2) Export traces and logs to your SIEM/Datadog via S3 or direct exporter (we have a datadog sink for logs/metrics) 3) You can attach custom trace ids in request headers and we propagate them. We'll also provide a sample tracing hook to include in your proxy.
[06:10] Maya: on the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoff — our goal is predictable latency at scale and data isolation. Dedicated seems attractive but cost is a concern. any quick numbers on per-token cost difference?
[06:22] Samir: ballpark: Dedicated reduces per-token infra markup but has a monthly reserved cost; Hosted is higher per-token but no commit. we'll send concrete numbers tailored to your QPS. also Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/quantization to reduce unit cost.- note that numbers vary by model and quantization profile.
[06:46] Derek: kernel selection / quantization question — if we pick a quantized model for cost, will you still support our current KV cache semantics? some of our chains depend on long context caching.
[06:58] Leah: we support KV cache across model variants; quantized variants might have different memory/perf tradeoffs. our runtime manages KV cache and will surface metrics on cache hit rates. for very long contexts we can recommend offloading to optimized pipelines or using chunked retrieval.
[07:20] Maya: can we do A/B between a hosted model and dedicated variant during pilot so we can compare latency?
[07:27] Samir: yes — common pattern: route a % of traffic to Hosted and rest to Dedicated via our routing policy; we can do canary or A/B. we also support automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
[07:38] Priya: encryption — you mentioned KMS integration. do you support customer-managed KMS (CMK) from AWS?
[07:47] Leah: yes, we support CMKs for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can integrate with your KMS with an enterprise plan. keys are used for data at rest encryption; we can also enable envelope encryption for sensitive payloads.
[08:05] Derek: proxy pattern question — we want to augment prompts with metadata server-side before calling Redwood. if the proxy adds metadata to prompt, does Redwood see those attributes in traces?
[08:16] Leah: any header or metadata you send we can echo back in logs/traces if you pass a trace-id or user-id header. we don't store it unless you opt into retention. we'll document the header contract.
[08:32] Omar: rate-limiting on our side needs to be able to circuit-break if Redwood returns 429 — do you have recommended retry/backoff semantics?
[08:41] Leah: yes recommended pattern: exponential backoff with jitter, treat 429 as retryable with capped attempts, and use tokens per-request for idempotency. we have a small library in the SDK that implements recommended backoff and circuit-breaker policy which you can plug into your proxy.
[09:00] [20+ minute block of technical Q&A — excerpts]
[09:05] Derek: during POC we'll want to run a throughput test: roughly 200 qps sustained with bursts to 600 qps, average generation length 120 tokens. is that realistic on Dedicated?
[09:18] Leah: yes that's within typical Dedicated capacity; we'll size GPU pool recommendations based on tokens/sec and model choice. please send actual workload traces and we'll run a simulated bench.
[09:33] Derek: do you support a private control plane option? our security team likes the idea that the control plane doesn't leave our VPC for audit logs.
[09:42] Samir: yes Private deployment includes a customer-managed control plane or on-prem option; most customers pick Private when they need total control over audit logs and network egress.
[09:55] Maya: what's the onboarding timeline to get a Dedicated pilot up? we need infra changes and cert approvals.
[10:02] Samir: typical pilot (bench + small prod slice) is 2–6 weeks depending on security review and network peering. for a fast start we often do a hosted pilot with dedicated endpoints later.
[10:16] Priya: can you also support per-request field-level redaction before logs are stored? we need PII redaction for support transcripts.
[10:25] Leah: yes — we have server-side redaction rules and the ability to scrub fields before storage; we can also configure no-retention for transcripts.
[10:36] Derek: how do we integrate with LlamaIndex vector stores? does your embeddings endpoint return standard vectors? latency numbers?
[10:46] Leah: embeddings are standard float vectors; we return dimensionality metadata and recommend vector normalization choices. latency depends on model; embedding calls are typically lower-lat than generation, but we'll include p50/p95 numbers for the models you care about.
[10:58] Maya: are there any gotchas with LangChain memory modules and Redwood streaming? we had some tokenization mismatch in the past with other providers.
[11:09] Leah: tokenization mismatch can happen if different tokenizer versions are used. we publish tokenizer info per model and provide a tokenizer library in the SDK. for memory modules we recommend using the SDK's encoding helpers.
[11:26] Derek: about quotas — can we set quotas per Workspace and limit specific routes (e.g., embeddings route separate from generation)?
[11:35] Samir: yes, Console allows route-level quotas and per-workspace API keys; you can set soft/hard caps and alerts.
[11:45] Maya: okay onto a nitty-gritty: we sometimes use long-running chat sessions with KV cache hot-starts, will Redwood allow us to pin model versions and ensure rollout safety when you push model updates?
[11:58] Leah: yes — model version pinning and rollout policies are part of the platform: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to previous version on regressions. Redwood Optimize can run evals on a prompt set to detect regressions.
[12:18] [Short silence; note of typing]
[12:27] Derek: for the POC, what logs do you need from our side? request patterns, token distributions, and any sample prompts?
[12:35] Leah: request patterns and token distribution are the most useful. sample prompts (anonymized) help for evaluation. also share your current batching and prompt templates.
[12:46] Maya: do you have an SDK snippet for a kong plugin to forward auth to Redwood?
[12:54] Leah: we have a sample kong plugin we can share; it demonstrates header injection, trace-id passthrough, and optional caching.
[13:07] Omar: curious about fallback policies: if Dedicated is down do you fall back to Hosted? is there automatic state sync for cache?
[13:18] Leah: you can configure automatic fallback to Hosted compatible model variants; KV cache isn't automatically migrated across clusters, so for warm starts we recommend application layer replication or a shared cache that the proxy manages.
[13:34] Maya: what about billing granularity and attribution per product team? we need clear per-team token cost reporting.
[13:42] Samir: Console provides per-api-key and per-route billing reports, token counts, and cost attribution. you can export billing to CSV or integrate with your billing system via API.
[13:55] [Wrap-up Q&A and decision signals]
[14:05] Maya: overall we like the Dedicated approach but want the Private option in case security review demands it. next step for us is internal approval and a security review — Priya will lead that.
[14:15] Priya: yes i'll compile a list of security items — SOC2 report, network diagrams, KMS key flow, SSO config, and retention options.
[14:23] Samir: we'll send SOC2, SSO guide, network topology, and the LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets. Leah will lead the bench.
[14:33] Leah: i'll prepare a benchmark plan: we'll need Derek's workload trace, target qps, and model choices. i'll also attach the SDK example for kong and the kong plugin.
[14:45] Derek: we'll try to get you the traces this week. also we'll list specific eval prompts for Redwood Optimize.
[14:55] Samir: perfect. i'll follow up with pricing for Dedicated and a pilot contract.
[15:05] Maya: sounds good — thank you both.
